# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **fill every non-wall zero inside each framed chamber with that frame’s gate color**, without testing reachability. It fits all five canonical demonstration pairs because every canonical chamber’s non-wall interior is four-connected. The eight-neighbor flood shortcut also fits all five, but “fill all” is simpler and therefore the stronger competing explanation.

An exact disagreement input is retained at `repo/generators/2d59c1b766d5/counterexamples/sealed_fill_all.json`. It is generated with seed `2401`, sample index `1`, and overrides `{"grid_h": 15, "grid_w": 20, "profile": "sealed"}`. A full-span gray wall divides each frame. The intended output fills only the gate-side component; the shortcut also paints the sealed-off zeros. The retained selected-Racket output and shortcut output differ in 28 cells.

I checked the answer by applying the selected canonical Racket rule through the public `Catalog.apply` runtime, requiring a matching catalog rule hash, no execution error, and a valid output. The independent Python four-neighbor mirror matches that Racket output. Focused tests regenerate the exact input from its seed/overrides and compare both named outputs byte-for-byte.

Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases deliberately. `sealed` occurs at every sample index congruent to 1 modulo 3. It also emits `diagonal` cases at residue 2; `repo/generators/2d59c1b766d5/counterexamples/diagonal_joint_witness.json` refutes both fill-all and eight-neighbor flood. A six-pair lesson contains each profile twice, so any single query holdout leaves a counterexample to every declared rival among the demonstrations.
